messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: The interactions that matter most are medicines that also slow the heart.
The interactions that matter most are medicines that block the liver enzyme CYP2D6.
This enzyme raises metoprolol levels in your blood.
Digoxin, clonidine, diltiazem, and verapamil.
These all slow the heart's electrical signal and heart rate.
Taking Digoxin, clonidine, diltiazem, and verapamil with metoprolol raises the risk of a very slow heartbeat.
Clonidine, when stopping either medicine.
You take both medications.
Metoprolol is stopped several days before clonidine is slowly withdrawn.
Beta blockers can worsen the blood pressure rebound that follows clonidine withdrawal.
Clonidine withdrawal causes a blood pressure rebound.
Quinidine, fluoxetine, paroxetine, and propafenone.
These strong CYP2D6 blockers double the amount of metoprolol in your blood.
Quinidine tripled levels of one form of metoprolol and doubled how long metoprolol lasted.
Weaker CYP2D6 blockers are likely to raise levels too.
Reserpine and MAO inhibitors.
These deplete adrenaline-type chemicals.
These can add to metoprolol's effect.
Triples: [["metoprolol", "interacts with", "medicines that slow the heart"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "medicines that block the liver enzyme CYP2D6"], ["CYP2D6", "affects", "metoprolol levels in blood"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "digoxin"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "clonidine"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "diltiazem"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "verapamil"], ["digoxin", "slows", "heart's electrical signal and heart rate"], ["clonidine", "slows", "heart's electrical signal and heart rate"], ["diltiazem", "slows", "heart's electrical signal and heart rate"], ["verapamil", "slows", "heart's electrical signal and heart rate"], ["taking metoprolol with digoxin", "raises risk of", "very slow heartbeat"], ["taking metoprolol with clonidine", "raises risk of", "very slow heartbeat"], ["taking metoprolol with diltiazem", "raises risk of", "very slow heartbeat"], ["taking metoprolol with verapamil", "raises risk of", "very slow heartbeat"], ["clonidine", "interacts with", "metoprolol"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "quinidine"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "fluoxetine"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "paroxetine"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "propafenone"], ["quinidine", "blocks", "CYP2D6"], ["fluoxetine", "blocks", "CYP2D6"], ["paroxetine", "blocks", "CYP2D6"], ["propafenone", "blocks", "CYP2D6"], ["quinidine", "increases", "metoprolol levels in blood"], ["quinidine", "increases", "metoprolol duration"], ["weaker CYP2D6 blockers", "likely to raise", "metoprolol levels"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "reserpine"], ["metoprolol", "interacts with", "MAO inhibitors"], ["reserpine", "depletes", "adrenaline-type chemicals"], ["MAO inhibitors", "deplete", "adrenaline-type chemicals"], ["reserpine", "adds to", "metoprolol's effect"], ["MAO inhibitors", "adds to", "metoprolol's effect"]]
Relations: ["adds to", "affects", "blocks", "deplete", "depletes", "increases", "interacts with", "likely to raise", "raises risk of", "slows"]
Answer:

completion:
adds to: The subject substance enhances or intensifies the effect of the object entity.  
affects: The subject entity influences or alters the levels or activity of the object entity.  
blocks: The subject substance inhibits or prevents the function of the object entity.  
deplete: The subject entity reduces or diminishes the levels of the object entity.  
depletes: The subject substance reduces or diminishes the levels of the object entity.  
increases: The subject entity raises or enhances the levels or duration of the object entity.  
interacts with: The subject drug has a pharmacological interaction with the object entity, potentially altering its effects.  
likely to raise: The subject entity is expected to increase or elevate the levels of the object entity.  
raises risk of: The subject action or combination increases the likelihood of the adverse event or condition specified by the object entity.  
slows: The subject entity reduces or delays the activity or function of the object entity.
